name: Willie Nelson
hook: A Texas songwriter who wrote 'Crazy' for Patsy Cline, grew tired of Nashville's string-heavy production, and won the right to release albums so bare his label thought they were demos.
blurb: Willie Nelson was born in Abbott, Texas, on 29 April 1933. He wrote his first song at seven and worked as a radio DJ in Texas and the Pacific Northwest while trying to sell songs. In 1960 he moved to Nashville, where Pamper Music hired him as a songwriter, and he wrote hits for other singers: 'Hello Walls', 'Funny How Time Slips Away' and 'Crazy' for Patsy Cline, which he said was hard to sell because it used more chords than the usual three. His own records on RCA, many produced by Chet Atkins, were given the Nashville sound, with strings and backing choirs, which he thought was mostly unnecessary. In 1972 he moved back to Texas, to Austin, signed to Atlantic with Jerry Wexler in 1973, and became a leader of 'outlaw country', a reaction against the Nashville sound's polished, conservative rules. His next label, Columbia, gave him complete control, and 'Red Headed Stranger' (May 1975), recorded in Garland, Texas, was so bare, just guitar, piano and drums, that the bosses thought it was a demo. They released it as it was, and it was a huge hit. In 1978 he made 'Stardust', an album of old pop standards, produced by his neighbour in Malibu, Booker T. Jones, who had led the Stax house band in Memphis; it stayed on the country album chart for a decade. In 1990 the tax authority, the IRS, seized his property over $32 million in unpaid taxes. He co-chairs the advisory board of NORML, which campaigns to legalise marijuana. He is still recording.
